key_insight: Dilute nitrogen incorporation in epitaxial LaFeO3 couples defect reconstruction and electronic changes to nearly 100-fold higher initial water-oxidation activity.
engineering_relevance: Coupled anion and vacancy engineering offers a route to more active earth-abundant oxide electrocatalysts, although this study concerns water oxidation rather than solar cells or AI.
method: Grow epitaxial LaFeO3-xNy films using nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed laser deposition.
Characterize structural, chemical, transport, and oxygen-evolution behavior.
Use ab initio calculations to evaluate coupled nitrogen–oxygen-vacancy–iron-vacancy configurations.
evidence_signal: At <0.8% N/O, films exhibit lattice expansion, predominantly bulk Fe3+, and nearly two orders of magnitude higher initial OER activity than undoped LaFeO3; calculations reproduce the expansion with a plausible charge-balanced defect model.
watch_item: The highly active as-grown state is metastable: near-surface nitrogen depletion and metallic-iron oxidation/removal accompany rapid initial activity decay.
paper_title: Nitrogen Defect Coupling in Epitaxial LaFeO3 From Structural Reconstruction to Water Oxidation
